scope: Theorem 4.1 (Tube, lattice, and pairing) of the manuscript “Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five” (preprints/Ambiently-homeomorphic-isolated-hypersurface-germs-in-C4-with-multiplicities-four-and-five-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 059 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7b9c31dcfb1ba9b7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For sufficiently large a, b satisfying (a − 2)α k > L0, (b − 2)β k > L0, where L0 = 4 is the gradient exponent in (3.1), and for sufficiently small s > 0, the germ fs : Cs → C has its sole critical point at the origin in a fixed small tube. Its integral Milnor lattice, in rational coordinates, is Λπ = {(pr l, z) : l ∈ D, z ∈ H ⊗ E, π∗l mod kH = (1 ⊗ τ)z} ⊂ KQ ⊕ (H ⊗ E)Q. (4.1) The rational orthogonal filling form on these coordinates is −sd|K ⊥ (sh ⊗ e). (4.2) The lattice and form are those of a genuine local Milnor page of fs in the smooth ambient germ Cs.
